correctness.rationale: The common binary stress diagonalizes the linear Fourier equation, and symmetric Markov ergodicity gives negative sample growth on each nonzero mode. The exact tilted-generator formula (also well known from older telegraph literature) yields the moment exponent. Strict convexity of the amplitude frontier and a unique positive cubic root yield the continuum critical order. On a periodic circle the admissible wave numbers form a positive lattice, and minimization of the mode-wise critical order is finite. Near the first admissible length only the fundamental mode contributes, giving an explicit simple pole. For long circles, a nondegenerate minimizing wave number and uniform nearest-lattice Taylor comparison yield the quadratic oscillatory asymptotic, including its liminf/limsup. The packaged standard-library verifier passed 2979 finite deterministic assertions; none substitutes for analytical proof.

value.rationale: A physically natural question in active-surface buckling is which modes and which statistical moments can grow on a finite experimental specimen. This complete theorem determines the moment threshold and finite wavelength band, then adds a sharp minimal specimen circumference at which no moment can grow below it, a divergent critical order just above it, and an explicit oscillatory finite-size correction at large circumference. These geometry-dependent cutoffs are exact, not minor numerical refinements, and separate infinite-surface ensemble statements from observable finite-spectrum effects. The known single-mode intermittency mechanism is not counted as the new value. Caveats: no nonlinear buckling or spatially local disorder.
